headline: European Council Proposes New Tax On Major Digital Companies
seoTitle: Antonio Costa Proposes New Digital Tech Tax For EU Budget
metaDescription: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a new 3% tax on global tech giants as part of a revised budget plan, which France has rejected.
aiSummaryBullets: European Council President Antonio Costa introduced a 2028-2034 budget proposal featuring a 3% levy on major digital companies.
The tax would apply to firms with annual digital activity revenue of €50 million in the EU and €750 million globally.
The French government has expressed opposition to the plan, stating that the proposal is insufficient.
aiContextParagraph: European Council President Antonio Costa has unveiled a draft proposal for the European Union's 2028-2034 budget. The plan suggests implementing a 3% tax on large digital corporations as a mechanism to reduce the financial contributions required from member states. According to the proposal, the tax would target companies that meet specific revenue criteria, including an annual turnover from digital operations of at least €50 million within the European Union and a total global turnover exceeding €750 million. While the proposal aims to restructure funding for the bloc, it has already faced pushback. Officials in France have formally rejected the draft, characterizing the current plan as inadequate. This development marks the beginning of complex negotiations regarding the long-term fiscal framework of the European Union, as member states continue to evaluate the implications of new digital taxation strategies on their national contributions.
whyItIsViral: This proposal is gaining attention after being covered by two independent outlets, reflecting the significance of upcoming EU fiscal negotiations.
